Beemo: Benchmark of Expert-edited Machine-generated Outputs

paper.arxiv.2411.04032

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2411.04032v3. Expert editing and limited detector/prompt-generalization discussion establish human/model data construction scope. Recommended edits and measured editing proportions remain distinct. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The study has no human detection baseline and does not evaluate commercial/API detectors; results can depend on editing prompts and may not transfer from expert editing to non-expert users.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Beemo uses expert editors to refine machine outputs for factual accuracy, style, coherence and fluency; two lead editors manually validate submissions and annotators may skip already-suitable or substantially unsuitable examples.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Beemo reports 25 native-English expert annotators and two lead editors, with an average pay rate of $20 per hour for the expert-based annotation process. It contains 2,187 underlying instances with nine text versions each, totaling 19,683 texts.
